issue_context.title: Svelte 5: Functions created with `$state` and passed to event handlers don't get updated
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Intended behaviour is for a button to have a _dynamic_ handler, that will change based on some other state.

[Reproduction](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE3VSwWrcMBD9lanowQte-9QWzNrQW0IOgSaQQ9WDbY1tpfLISPImi_G_F0ne7CahJ6HRe2_mvdHCOqnQsuL3wqgekRXs5zSxlLnT5C_2iMohS5nVs2l95WBbIydXceJOjpM2DhawrnYIK3RGj8BZlksS-JpFdvZsOeN0yC9MOkiaZgeNJFEcazVjuQSNTNSuziYjW1whj9Av-z083f-6e4Cn28cbeLy5fYD9vtpeDs3snCbQ1CrZ_i2XZAdlFSfKhpqEQpN1lOzWKrI4faJ8BK_B3YfyiNbWPa7eSRTwIzQmvzqEPFbtUFOP4AYEmscGDTgNP9JQ2BrbQc9KgK1PMMh-SH0dXqRSoHQPnCn9wtkh92osZaMWspMoWOHMjGv6tqnrkC8re7bX62o1WQc-VSjha3CULN5dyLiAb5zWnQ8lAjezHivQyCOKrDklMdJAk11yWRFU8N2TnUE3G4oI7rakCuDM2-MsjfWOCohSvplWmCndJ2dQEFoj8r3eO8WQTXp--J9kQJ0Vo0FO-Bq-a3Qav2wZe3hLQbPHtwySHSywDXKOxYt93sif9R8AzQCWRwMAAA==)

The button's onclick does not get recomputed when the function changes (does change in the state).

Can be fixed by just wrapping the function with an anonymous function, as seen in the comment of the repl.

[More minimal reproduction](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE21Sy26DMBD8le2qB5CA3BEgJadEPVRqIuVQ90DBgFOzRthUiRD_XhlHeTQ5WV7PzM7ueMRKSK4x_hyR8pZjjMuuwwDNqbMX_cul4RigVkNf2Eqii150JmPEjGg71RsYQZvccJig6lULDKOFoJIfI8eODpoho2RxZVLyEoawf_9428J-s1vDbr3ZQhhm55fkezBGESgqpCh-0tHzIc1cm6jMTR5V5PlTdqb8R9_hptmqVLW14JDPOK6Dd0eFFFy5UKSV5JFUtcdwxdD3nWzR5FRzqOhO3Mr3i-xyMNcETMOBobWC4MAB6EYNsgSpamC4tIu6xV71Hxik-jaX8nSmrhgGoI2Q0ha0E8MAW1WKSvASY9MPfAouOd9GdA38oG_DtnMbsNuAFF7n3Xijnbui-Olqlgx9RpNvZ-bH-Xc4DfdDUpjZVpDR9Ojua_oD89FWWJECAAA=), but I think the first one illustrates the real world scenario better.

comments: Event handlers passed to DOM elements are static. So passing an event handler that might dynamically change isn't supported. We need to add some docs for this I guess. As you did, wrapping the event handler in an arrow function is the correct thing to do here.

> Event handlers passed to DOM elements are static. So passing an event handler that might dynamically change isn't supported. We need to add some docs for this I guess. As you did, wrapping the event handler in an arrow function is the correct thing to do here.

@trueadm 
is it only true for event handlers? or for all "native" html props of stuff?
also, any reason why it can't be made reactive? just curious to understand.

@trueadm [this does work though?](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAE22OwWrDQAxEf0WIHGwwCcnRtQO55CeyObhrrbt0IxmvHAjG_17WqWkhOY40b2YmdD5QxPIyITc3whJPfY8F6qNPIt4pKGGBUcbBpksV7eB7PRo2GkjBMdSwidooZVkO9RGscJRA2yBdts_zD8PJ60a26oXBfjXc0ZmzHKb0MLpEvLKHBdXZcLX7K-Xqc1QVBmEbvP2upzVwXjY9Fax1CX4C72H3iwXp_lmxwJu03nlqsdRhpPk6_wBlUu0vKwEAAA==)

Edit: did you mean that event handlers passed to dom are static IF the functions are exported from another file?
Because it also works when passing a callback (that can change) from a parent to a child as a prop, and putting it on a button.
```html
<button onclick={callback} />
```
Hmm that's a good point. Let me look into that logic again.

review_comments: Not sure if this has any effect in practise, but I think it would be better to make this `(binding.declaration_kind === 'import' && handler.type === 'MemberExpression')` so that this does not apply the dynamic handler stuff to identifier imports
Why not though? Imports can be live bindings, thus dynamic too? This is the only change in their PR too.
